claims.claim: Deere's precision-ag stack connects cameras/ML, targeted application and Operations Center data to the farmer need for lower chemical/input intensity and labor/productivity gains; this is a real technology-to-human-need bridge rather than a pure equipment-cycle claim.

The causal path remains exposed to farm economics: Deere Financial's lower agriculture-and-turf receivables reflect reduced equipment demand, so precision adoption can strengthen product value without eliminating replacement-cycle sensitivity.

causalEdges.mechanism: real-time weed identification and nozzle-level application
reduced chemical use and operator burden
customer purchasing capacity and fleet replacement timing

risks.risk: Precision technology improves unit economics but does not remove agricultural cyclicality or farmer-capex sensitivity.

unknowns.unknown: Independent long-duration evidence on realized whole-farm ROI across crops/geographies remains limited in this run.

claims.claim: The strongest falsifier is not technology failure but economic transmission: agriculture-and-turf financing balances remain lower because equipment demand has been reduced, while the parent filing notes construction credit-loss pressure and continued cost pressure.
Deere's cycle-bottom statement should remain a hypothesis until improved orders translate into sustained production-agriculture revenue and healthier customer financing metrics.

risks.risk: Financing exposure transmits weak farm/construction economics into credit losses and can amplify equipment-cycle weakness.
Pricing can offset some costs but higher production/material costs can still compress margins.

unknowns.unknown: Whether 2026 truly marks the agricultural-equipment trough remains forward-looking rather than established fact.
